idiom_name: struct per table with an embedded base struct plus a hand-written join
implementation_notes: Go has no inheritance, so a hierarchy becomes one struct per table with the base struct embedded (or exposed through an interface), and the joined read is written out with database/sql - or generated ahead of time with sqlc, which reads the schema and produces the row types. What replaces the classic mapper is a load function per type that scans base and subtype columns from one JOIN and returns the composed struct, while polymorphic handling is a type column and a switch rather than a vtable. No mainstream Go ORM maps a joined hierarchy, so the hand-written form is the normal choice; the joined schema can still be worth it for the NOT NULL and foreign key guarantees it buys.
pitfalls: Embedding copies values, so the same logical object loaded twice yields two distinct Party values - compare the key, never the struct.
Scanning into sql.NullString/NullTime for columns that a sibling type owns turns a wrong join into a silent zero value; scan into non-nullable types so the error surfaces.
